title: Declare abstract Gherkin narrative in every acceptance given/when/then section

facts.note: Acceptance documents identified by file kind / acceptance path pattern; the rule constrains every acceptance section regardless of how it is reached.
Applies whenever an acceptance section is authored, edited (any part of the document) or reviewed/validated, including existing acceptances.
Planner tasks that author, revise or review acceptances.
Schema check over given.abstract / when.abstract / then.abstract (presence, type, minItems/minLength) on acceptance documents; no such detector exists yet.

fires: Planner authors a new acceptance whose given/when/then sections carry only structured machine fields and no abstract narrative.
Planner edits an acceptance (in any part, e.g. identity metadata) whose then.abstract is an empty list.
An existing acceptance under review has when.abstract as a list or as a string shorter than 5 characters.
An acceptance's given.abstract item bundles several preconditions into one line.
doesNotFire: Plans, wagons or docs that contain no acceptance given/when/then sections.
Code or test files produced from acceptances (the rule governs the acceptance document, not generated tests).

given: An acceptance document with given/when/then sections exists or is being written.
when: You author, edit or review that acceptance.
then: Every section must carry all three REQUIRED abstract fields: given.abstract (non-empty list of strings, each item a single precondition/setup state), when.abstract (string ≥5 chars, present tense, clear actor and action), then.abstract (non-empty list of strings, each item a single observable outcome).
prefer: Keep abstract fields alongside the structured fields in the same section: abstract for stakeholders (Gherkin), structured for machines (test generation).
Use identity.purpose as the scenario name; a separate top-level name is not needed.
avoid: Omitting any abstract field or leaving given/then lists empty.
Bundling several preconditions or outcomes into one item.
Replacing structured machine fields with the narrative (they coexist).
Placeholder text that passes length/count checks without describing a real state, action or outcome.
why: Abstract Gherkin narrative makes each acceptance readable by stakeholders while structured fields stay machine-consumable for test generation.
evidence: Every acceptance section has given.abstract as array[str] with minItems 1, and each item states a single precondition/setup state (required, not optional).
Every acceptance section has when.abstract as str with minLength 5, present tense, with a clear actor and action.
Every acceptance section has then.abstract as array[str] with minItems 1, each item a single observable outcome.
identity.purpose serves as the scenario name; a separate top-level name is unnecessary (its presence is not itself a violation).
verifier_detail: Schema: given.abstract: array[str], minItems 1, REQUIRED — each item a single precondition/setup state; when.abstract: str, minLength 5, REQUIRED — present tense, clear actor and action; then.abstract: array[str], minItems 1, REQUIRED — each item a single observable outcome.

Term abstract_field: a Gherkin narrative line within a given/when/then section, for stakeholder readability alongside the structured machine fields. Locations: given.abstract, when.abstract, then.abstract.

Source shape examples — given.abstract: ["appendix.convention.yaml defines manifest structure", "User account exists in the database"]; when.abstract: "User submits login form with credentials"; then.abstract: ["Wagon manifest includes appendices: [] at root level", "Resolver can resolve appendix paths using URN pattern"].
Presence, type and size checks are mechanical; item atomicity (single precondition / single outcome), present tense and clear actor/action are mandatory but LLM-judged.
